findings.title: Shared err variable written from concurrent index builds can swallow errors
findings.body: In init, the errgroup closure writes the outer err (declared at line 181) and increments totalBatchesIndexed (line 189) from up to initWorkers goroutines at once. The closure returns that shared variable, so a failing build can be overwritten by another goroutine's successful s.build (which sets err to nil) before the closure's return value is read. group.Wait() then reports nil and startup continues with a namespace's index missing. The race detector also flags this. Because init now runs synchronously inside NewResourceServer, a swallowed error means the server starts with incomplete search results. Use a closure-local err and an atomic or mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: Constructor now performs DB init and full index build synchronously with no deadline
findings.body: NewResourceServer now synchronously runs lifecycle.Init (for the sql backend: DB provider init and ping) and the full search index build via search.init, then returns any failure as a constructor error. The context is a background context with no deadline, so a slow or unreachable database, or a long index build, now blocks construction indefinitely instead of failing individual RPCs. Any dependency-injection graph that constructs ResourceServer now runs this I/O at construction time, before service Init phases, and fails startup on any init error. The PR does not show that every caller constructs it after the database is ready. Add a startup timeout and confirm construction order for all callers.

findings.title: Lazy-to-eager init change ships with no tests
findings.body: The change removes the Init guard from about ten handlers, reorders initialization (search init now runs before initWatcher), and makes NewResourceServer fail on init errors. No unit tests are added or updated; the only test touched adds a postgres skip. Nothing verifies that the constructor returns the init error, that the broadcaster is ready for Watch immediately after construction, or that mocked backends in existing server tests tolerate the eager GetResourceStats, WatchWriteEvents and lifecycle calls now made during construction.

findings.title: Watch consumer does not check channel close and panics on nil event during shutdown
findings.body: The goroutine consuming the watch channel does 'v := <-events' without checking the ok flag. The sql backend's poller closes its stream when the backend is stopped (deferred close after <-b.done), so after Stop every receive yields nil. handleEvent then dereferences evt.Type on its first line and panics in a background goroutine, which takes down the process during graceful shutdown. The context used here is context.Background() and is never cancelled, so nothing stops the loop. This predates the PR, but it is the init path the PR changes and now runs at construction. Check ok and return when the channel closes.

findings.title: Missing indexes are still built under the gRPC request context
findings.body: The PR's goal is to stop index builds from being cancelled by request contexts, but Search still builds any index missing from the cache with the request context: Search calls getOrCreateIndex(ctx), which calls s.build(ctx, key, 10, 0), which calls BuildIndex(ctx) and ListIterator(ctx). Namespaces skipped at startup (count at or below InitMinCount) and namespaces created after startup still take this path, so a client disconnect or deadline mid-build still aborts the build. The hard-coded size of 10 is also far below any realistic FileThreshold, so these indexes are always memory-only even when large. Build missing indexes with a server-lifetime context, or document that this path remains request-scoped.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without taking cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. The PR adds a TotalDocs call to searchSupport.init (search.go line 216) that runs right after the watch goroutine starts, and that goroutine can call BuildIndex for a namespace with no index yet. A concurrent map iteration and map write is a fatal, unrecoverable runtime error in Go, so this can crash the process. Take cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Removing the build lock lets duplicate builds for the same key run concurrently
findings.body: Removing cacheMu from BuildIndex means concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource now run in parallel, and nothing dedupes them (the TODO in getOrCreateIndex notes this gap). Two concurrent Search requests on a new namespace each run a full build, roughly doubling CPU and memory for that namespace. For file indexes, the second caller gets bleve's path-exists error from bleve.New at this line while the first build is still in flight. The old lock did not dedupe either, but it serialized the work. The speedup holds only for distinct keys, so the PR should add per-key deduplication or state this limitation.

findings.title: Post-Stop rejection of RPCs was lost when the Init guards were removed
findings.body: Previously every RPC called s.Init, which returned s.initErr, and Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', so RPCs after Stop were rejected. With the Init guards removed from Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob and GetBlob, nothing reads initErr after construction. This assignment is now dead, and requests arriving after Stop are served against a stopped service: writes still reach the database and watch streams run on a cancelled context. Keep a post-stop check in the handlers or document the new behavior.

findings.title: Constructor error path does not release context or lifecycle resources
findings.body: When Init fails, NewResourceServer logs and returns without calling s.cancel() or stopping the lifecycle. The background context and any resources opened by lifecycle.Init (for the sql backend, the DB handle from dbProvider.Init) are never released. Now that construction performs real I/O, the error path should clean up, for example by calling s.cancel() and stopping the lifecycle when Init fails.

findings.title: WriteEvent discards the span context, so the PR's trace fix is incomplete
findings.body: The PR claims to fix trace propagation, but only GetResourceStats was changed to use the derived context. WriteEvent still does '_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)' and then passes the original ctx to create/update/delete, so those spans become siblings of the WriteEvent span rather than children. The same pattern remains in ReadResource (line 353) and ListIterator (line 388). Either fix all of them or stop describing the trace propagation as fixed.

findings.title: BuildIndex span context is discarded, so the span has no children
findings.body: BuildIndex starts its span with '_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)' and never passes the derived context to bleve.New, the builder, or the flush. The span therefore has no children, which is inconsistent with the trace-propagation fix this PR describes in search.go's build and init. Use 'ctx, span :=' and pass ctx onward.

findings.title: Poller span is never ended on the listLatestRVs error path
findings.body: In poller, the span started at line 580 is ended only at the bottom of the tick. The error branch at lines 583-586 logs, resets the ticker, and executes 'continue' without calling span.End(), so the span is never ended and is never exported on every failed tick. Call span.End() before continue, or end the span in each branch.

findings.title: Postgres skip removes the only storage-server startup test for postgres runs
findings.body: This skip disables TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer for every postgres run. That test exercises the storage-server startup path that this PR moves into the NewResourceServer constructor, so the PR now has no coverage of that path on postgres. The skip is unrelated to the PR description, has no tracking issue, and removes coverage rather than fixing the test. Link an issue or keep the test running.
